add_action('plugins_loaded', function () {
    if (!did_action('elementor/loaded')) {
        return;
    }

    // Register widgets
    add_action('elementor/widgets/register', function ($widgets_manager) {
        require_once WP21_EL_PATH . 'widgets/class-dia-text-widget.php';
        require_once WP21_EL_PATH . 'widgets/class-typewriter-widget.php';

        $widgets_manager->register(new \WP21_GradientButton_Widget());
        $widgets_manager->register(new \WP21_TextGlitch_Widget());
        $widgets_manager->register(new \WP21_TextReveal_Widget());
        $widgets_manager->register(new \WP21_TextCycle_Widget());
    });

    // Register widget category
    add_action('elementor/elements/categories_registered', function ($elements_manager) {
        $elements_manager->add_category('wp21-animations', [
            'title' => '21st Animations',
            'icon'  => 'fa fa-magic',
        ]);
    });

    // Enqueue assets
    add_action('wp_enqueue_scripts', function () {
        wp_enqueue_style(
            'wp21-widgets',
            WP21_EL_URL . 'assets/widgets.css',
            [],
            '1.0.0'

        $asset_file = WP21_EL_PATH . 'assets/frontend.asset.php';

        wp_enqueue_script(
            'wp21-frontend',
            WP21_EL_URL . 'assets/frontend.js',
            $deps,
            $version,
            true
        );
    });
});

<?php
defined('ABSPATH') || exit;

class WP21_GradientButton_Widget extends \Elementor\Widget_Base {

    public function get_name() {
        return 'wp21_gradient_button';
    }

    public function get_title() {
        return 'Gradient Button';
    }

    public function get_icon() {
        return 'eicon-button';
    }

    public function get_categories() {
        return ['wp21-animations'];
    }

    protected function register_controls() {
        $this->start_controls_section('content_section', [
            'label' => 'Content',
            'tab'   => \Elementor\Controls_Manager::TAB_CONTENT,
        ]);

        $this->add_control('button_text', [
            'label'   => 'Button Text',
            'type'    => \Elementor\Controls_Manager::TEXT,
            'default' => 'Get Started',
        ]);

        $this->add_control('url', [
            'label'   => 'Link URL',
            'type'    => \Elementor\Controls_Manager::URL,
            'dynamic' => ['active' => true],
            'default' => ['url' => ''],
        ]);

        $this->add_control('variant', [
            'label'   => 'Variant',
            'type'    => \Elementor\Controls_Manager::SELECT,
            'default' => 'default',
            'options' => [
                'default' => 'Default',
                'variant' => 'Variant',
            ],
        ]);

        $this->end_controls_section();
    }

    protected function render() {
        $settings    = $this->get_settings_for_display();
        $button_text = $settings['button_text'] ?? 'Get Started';
        $url         = $settings['url']['url'] ?? '';
        $variant     = $settings['variant'] ?? 'default';

        $btn_class = 'wp21-gradient-btn';
        if ($variant === 'variant') {
            $btn_class .= ' is-variant';
        }

        $tag   = !empty($url) ? 'a' : 'button';
        $href  = !empty($url) ? ' href="' . esc_url($url) . '"' : '';
        $rel   = !empty($url) ? ' rel="noopener noreferrer"' : '';
        $extra = '';
        if ($tag === 'a') {
            $extra .= $href . $rel;
        }

        echo '<' . $tag . ' class="' . esc_attr($btn_class) . '"' . $extra . '>';
        echo esc_html($button_text);
        echo '</' . $tag . '>';
    }
}

Wait, I just noticed something important: the page was rebuilt successfully ("OK 22791b" was the output from the script). But the page shows OLD content. This suggests one of:
1. Elementor cached the CSS and the old layout is being shown

Actually, looking at the post-23.css that's loaded: `href='http://localhost:8882/wp-content/uploads/elementor/css/post-23.css?ver=1784209599'` - this is a CSS file generated by Elementor. Actually, I think the problem is the time. The `post-23.css` has version `1784209599`. The PHP script did `update_post_meta($pid, '_elementor_data', wp_slash($data))`. But Elementor also stores a compiled CSS version. If the CSS wasn't regenerated, the old content might still be displayed.

So the `_elementor_data` is updated correctly (22791 bytes, has "Animated Components"). But the page renders the OLD content ("21st.dev Showcase"). This means Elementor is caching the rendered HTML output somewhere.

Option 1: Elementor caches the page HTML in a file

Let me check the post-23.css file. Elementor stores the rendered HTML structure within the CSS file as well in some cases. Let me check:

Actually, Elementor's CSS post file stores both CSS AND the full HTML structure. When you update `_elementor_data`, Elementor needs to regenerate the CSS file. My PHP script did try to call `$css_file->update()` but it was in the first script (rebuild-elo.php), not in the second one (rebuild-elo2.php).

Wait, looking at rebuild-elo2.php, I didn't include the CSS regeneration logic at the end. Let me trigger a regeneration.

Actually, the simplest fix is to just open the Elementor editor and save the page. But since the user can't open the link, let me regenerate the CSS via PHP.
The data is correct (22791 bytes, has "Animated Components") but Elementor's CSS cache still has the old layout. Let me regenerate it:

input.content:
<?php
require_once 'C:\Users\salma\Studio\21st-showcase\wp-load.php';
$pid = 23;

// Clear Elementor CSS cache
delete_post_meta($pid, '_elementor_css');

// Regenerate CSS
if (class_exists('Elementor\Core\Files\CSS\Post')) {
    try {
        $css_file = new \Elementor\Core\Files\CSS\Post($pid);
        $css_file->update();
        echo "CSS regenerated for page $pid\n";
    } catch (\Throwable $e) {
        echo "Error: " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
    }
} else {
    echo "Elementor CSS class not found\n";
}

// Also clear any Elementor cache
if (class_exists('Elementor\Plugin')) {
    try {
        \Elementor\Plugin::$instance->files_manager->clear_cache();
        echo "Elementor cache cleared\n";
    } catch (\Throwable $e) {
        echo "Cache clear error: " . $e->getMessage() . "\n";
    }
}

echo "Done\n";

The issue was missing Elementor element IDs in the JSON data — each section/column/widget needs an 8-char random `id` or Elementor can't render them. Fixed by using Elementor's `Document::save()` which properly generates all IDs.

**Now working:**
- Page renders at `http://localhost:8882/` with correct dark styles, all 10 sections, all 6 widget types
- Elementor editor opens at `http://localhost:8882/wp-admin/post.php?post=23&action=elementor`
- Can edit any widget's text, colors, gradients directly through Elementor

**Full page structure:**
1. Hero (100vh, "Animated Components" → h1 → subtitle)
2. Features (3 cards: Fluid Motion, Developer First, Customizable)
3. Dia Text (3 variants: blue/purple, warm, inline)
4. Typewriter (2 variants)
5. Gradient Button (default + variant)
6. Text Glitch (small + large)
7. Text Reveal (scroll-activated)
8. Text Cycle (simple + with prefix)
9. Combined Demo
10. Footer

All with `#111` bg, `#f6f3ec` text, `#9a958a` secondary, `#2b2a25` borders.
